newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Colombian rebels fire on Venezuelan army chopper.
newsitem.headline: Colombian rebels fire on Venezuelan army chopper.

text.p: Suspected Colombian guerrillas fired on a Venezuelan army helicopter after killing two Venezuelan soldiers earlier this week in the worst border incident in a year, Defence Minister Pedro Nicolas Valencia said on Friday.
Nobody was hurt in the helicopter shooting on Tuesday between the villages of Victoria and Guasdualito, in western Apure state.
"I can confirm the helicopter, a Super-Puma, was attacked" by Colombian rebels, the minister told reporters. A 5.56 mm bullet hit the rotor but nobody was injured, an army spokesman said.

The helicopter was carrying 12 people, including government officials dispatched to the area to investigate the deaths of the two soldiers. Valencia said about 30 rebels of the National Liberation Army (ELN), Colombia's second largest guerrilla force, carried out the attack on a patrol boat on Arauca river.

Tuesday's attack, the latest in a spate of border incidents, further strained relations between the two countries, with Venezuelan authorities strongly urging Colombia to boost its military presence in Arauca province and in the border town of Arauquita in particular.
"Arauquita and surrounding villages have become a sanctuary for the guerrillas, where they plan attacks against our forces and kidnappings of Venezuelan citizens," Valencia said.
Venezuela and Colombia share a 1,400 mile (2,200 km) porous border, where kidnapping, drug trafficking and smuggling have markedly increased in recent years.
